title: Comparing Experiences: képest, egyre, and the Full Toolkit

sections.title: Five lessons, one reflection
sections.content: You now have language for the whole arc of talking about an experience: whether it ever happened (*már*, *még soha nem*), whether it was a first (*először*), what it did to the person or thing it touched (participle adjectives like *elkészített*, *megérintett*), and how things have changed since (*azelőtt*, *azóta*, *ha visszatekintek*). Comparing experiences adds one more piece: putting two things — then and now, you and someone else — side by side.

sections.title: Comparison words
rows: than (you know it from A2 Unit 13)

items.spanish: A mai önbizalmamhoz képest, régen nagyon félénk voltam.
items.english: Compared to my confidence today, I used to be very shy.

items.spanish: Egyre bátrabb lettem, minél többször próbáltam ki új dolgokat.
items.english: I became increasingly braver, the more often I tried new things.

items.spanish: A mostani utam sokkal izgalmasabb volt, mint az első.
items.english: This trip was much more exciting than the first one.

items.spanish: Minél többször próbáltam, annál bátrabb lettem.
items.english: The more often I tried, the braver I became.

sections.content: *képest* always needs a noun in the -hoz/-hez/-höz case in front of it, even when that noun is just a pronoun like *ehhez* ("to this") or *ahhoz* ("to that") — *ehhez képest*, *ahhoz képest*, *a régi énemhez képest*. Leave that case ending off and *képest* has nothing to compare against. *minél* … *annál* pairs two comparatives: *minél többször*, *annál bátrabb* ("the more often, the braver").
